newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS RALLY IN THIRD PERIOD TO TIE CAPITALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS RALLY IN THIRD PERIOD TO TIE CAPITALS.

text.p: Ted Donato and Steve Staios scored in the third period and Bill Ranford made 42 saves as the Boston Bruins rallied for a 3-3 tie with the Washington Capitals Monday in a battle of two teams struggling to stay in the Eastern Conference playoff race.

Staios tied the game with 8:32 remaining on a brilliant individual effort. He burst between defenceman Sergei Gonchar and Brendan Witt before sliding a shot under goaltender Jim Carey, who dove out in an unsuccessful attempt to poke the puck off the stick of Staios.
"It was a huge individual effort for us and a huge goal," said Boston coach Steve Kasper. "Steve Staios came up in a big way on that goal."
All three Staios goals this season have come against the Capitals.

"We made a mistake on the third goal," said Washington coach Jim Schoenfeld. "It was a 1-on-2. He walked in and scored the goal. It was one mistake. For the one mistake we made, talk to the Boston people and see how many they made.
"There was a guy on the other end that made sure we only got one point ... Ranford played great," he added. "If you had to pick the difference in this game, it's pretty obvious it was Bill Ranford."
Despite the third-period heroics, the Bruins' winless streak reached 10 games (0-8-2), their longest since an 0-11-1 streak in 1965.
Rookie Anson Carter scored twice for Washington, which is winless in its last four games (0-3-1).

"It feels good, but it doesn't take away from the fact that we tied," said Carter, who had his first career two-goal effort. "We didn't get the win. I think right now we'll settle for the one point and try to build on this tie."

The Capitals, 19-2-3 when leading after two periods, had a 3-1 cushion entering the third. But with Witt serving a kneeing penalty, Donato put his own rebound past Carey for his 23rd goal of the season and eighth this month.
Jean-Yves Roy's goal 3:26 into the first period staked Boston to a 1-0 lead, but Carter tied it on the power play just over two minutes later, deflecting Gonchar's shot past Ranford.
Sylvain Cote cut down from the blue line, took a short centering pass from Steve Konowalchuk and lifted a shot over Ranford from close range to put Washington ahead with 3:13 to go in the period.
Carter gave the Caps a two-goal cushion at 3:41 of the second, chipping Jason Allison's centering pass past the glove of a sliding Ranford.

Andrew Brunette set up both of Carter's goals for Washington, which is 1-5-1 in its last seven home games but moved into a tie with Tampa Bay and Ottawa for ninth in the Eastern Conference with 53 points. The Bruins have 48 points.

"I made a couple of saves and got a little confidence back and the team seemed to rally around that," Ranford said. "We have to turn things around and I guess this is a start in the right direction. We battled hard and we haven't come back too many times when we've been down going into the third, so that was a big turnaround for us."

In Phoenix, Darren McCarty scored twice in a four-goal first period and Brendan Shanahan added his 39th and 40th goals as the Detroit Red Wings extended their unbeaten streak to five games with a 5-3 victory over the Coyotes.
Shanahan joined Mario Lemieux and Jaromir Jagr as the NHL's only 40-goal scorers. He also had a pair of assists to move into sixth place in the league with 71 points.
Vyacheslav Kozlov had the other goal for the Red Wings, who have lost just twice in their last 12 games (7-2-3) and squared the season series with Phoenix at 2-2-1.
Jeremy Roenick had two goals and an assist for the Coyotes, who were trying to win three straight home games for the first time this season.

Phoenix closed within 4-3 midway through the third period when Norm Maciver floated a shot from the inside edge of the right faceoff circle that appeared to deflect in off defenceman Nicklas Lidstrom's right shoulder.
Chris Osgood made 39 saves and Detroit killed off all seven Coyotes' power plays.
Phoenix goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin stopped 30 shots.
